phase: P7: sockets for ONLINE GAME on Linux
change: OriginalMacWinsock (BSD-socket Winsock 1.1, NETWORK_PLAY_PLAN.md N1) moved from NTSDMacPlatform to NTSDRuntime under its name and made portable (Darwin, Glibc, Musl); NTSDSDL uses it on every host and no longer needs --no-network
linuxDifferences: errno numbering: WSAE codes are 10000 + BSD errno; Linux errno values are mapped to the BSD numbers (Darwin unchanged)
SIGPIPE: MSG_NOSIGNAL on send instead of SO_NOSIGPIPE; no sin_len
Glibc imports SOCK_STREAM/MSG_* as enum types; the Winsock argument check now compares Winsock's numbers (AF_INET 2, SOCK_STREAM 1, IPPROTO_TCP 6), equal to Darwin's

readiness: the game selects (WSAAsyncSelect) before listen(); Linux epoll reports such an unconnected socket as hung up, which first delivered a spurious FD_ACCEPT (the game's own 'Accpet() Error' box at iteration 23) and, once ignored, left Dispatch no longer watching the descriptor (strace: host listened, client connected, host never accepted). On non-Darwin hosts watching now starts when listen/connect/accept has made the socket listening or connected, and FD_ACCEPT also requires poll() to show a pending connection. Darwin path unchanged.
